title: Which counts N admit a tiling of a triangle by N congruent copies of a triangle?

problemStatement.formal: Characterize \mathcal{N} = \{\, N \in \mathbb{N} : \exists\, \text{triangles } T, R \text{ with } T \text{ tiled by } N \text{ non-overlapping congruent copies of } R \,\}. In particular decide whether \mathcal{N} = \mathbb{N} or determine the exact forbidden counts, going beyond the square values N = k^2 (k \ge 1) supplied by the medial reptiling.
problemStatement.plain: If you cut a triangle into N smaller triangles that are all congruent to each other, which values of N are possible? Reptiling (repeated medial subdivision) shows every perfect square N = k^2 works for any triangle. Erdős #634 asks for the full set of achievable counts N — which non-square values are realizable and whether any count is forbidden for every triangle.
whyMatters: Resolves (or advances) the named open Erdős Problem #634 on dissecting triangles into congruent triangles.

Extends the fully verified parent proof of the k=2 square-reptiling base case to a global characterization of achievable tiling counts, linking elementary constructions to number-theoretic and isometry-group obstructions.

knownResults: Square reptiling: every triangle tiles into k^2 congruent 1/k-scale copies; the k=2 medial case is machine-checked in erdos-634-medial-congruence.
Strip/cevian constructions give a right triangle a tiling into m congruent triangles for every m, and special triangles (e.g. 30-60-90) admit N=3.
The exact achievable set N over all triangles, and whether N = ℕ, remains open.
references: S. L. Snover, C. Waiveris, J. K. Williams, Rep-tiling for triangles, Discrete Mathematics (1991)
